missing_information: References, acknowledgements and other labelled back matter excluded; body and detected appendices retained where budget permits.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are generally well supported by the reported results: reviewer-guided revision improves more than fixed-prompt self-revision, Stanford Reviewer independently confirms upward trajectories, and the execution-versus-idea resolution asymmetry is quantified and discussed. The abstract's headline numbers match the body, and the authors appropriately frame the finding that novelty concerns are rarely resolved.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is meaningful and multi-layered: reviewer quality is separately benchmarked against baselines on 650 ICLR papers with pairwise judging and human-alignment checks, and revision outcomes are measured on 30 papers across five domains with score trajectories, an external Stanford Reviewer evaluation of human-initialized revisions, and a weakness-resolution analysis (128/150 execution vs 2/18 idea weaknesses). Controls include autonomous self-revision with a fixed prompt and AI-initialized guidance, isolating the effect of iterative reviewer feedback.
primary.limitations: The evaluation set is small (30 papers) and constrained to ICLR papers reproducible on a single 96 GB GPU, with cost (~$65/paper) cited as the limiting factor. The same reviewer both guides and scores the reviewer-driven conditions, though the external Stanford Reviewer evaluation partially mitigates this circularity; Stanford Reviewer is not applied to the AI-initialized or self-revision conditions.
primary.method_assessment: The system design is described in adequate detail: the scientist retains full revision history and addresses each reviewer concern through code edits, literature search, experiment execution, and manuscript updates, while the reviewer independently evaluates only the current manuscript with no memory of prior drafts or scores. The reviewer uses a structured multi-phase process with deep literature search over an indexed arXiv corpus, temporal grounding, and a verification pass.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper makes a substantive, clearly scoped contribution with a well-described system, appropriate controls, independent external evaluation, and a nuanced characterization of what iterative revision can and cannot improve. The main weaknesses are acknowledged and bounded by the study design, and the evidence supports the stated claims without overclaiming.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces AppliedScientist, a closed-loop system that iteratively revises rejected papers' implementation, experiments, and manuscript under fresh independent AI reviews, while keeping the central research contribution fixed. It contributes a benchmark of reviewer-guided versus fixed-prompt self-revision across 30 ICLR papers and a characterization of which reviewer weaknesses revision can resolve.

The main weaknesses are acknowledged and bounded by the study design, and the evidence supports the stated claims without overclaiming.

The same reviewer both guides and scores the reviewer-driven conditions, though the external Stanford Reviewer evaluation partially mitigates this circularity; Stanford Reviewer is not applied to the AI-initialized or self-revision conditions.
